why.confound: EP-0005 found r_safe falling with pool size (0.8125 -> 0.5 for N = 32 -> 512) and I recorded that in Current Understanding v5. But I declared at seal time that the mix family confounds pool size with two other things that grow with N: the NUMBER OF BACKGROUND CLASSES (the background is every power of two up to N/2, so it grows as log N) and the NUMBER OF CONCURRENTLY RUNNING SMALL JOBS (roughly N / E[k], so it grows as N). Nothing in E7 separates the three.
why.stake: If the driver is the count of competing small jobs rather than pool size, then 'r_safe falls with pool size' is the wrong statement of the finding, and the practical rule in v5 ('use 0.8 for a 32-GPU pool and 0.5 for a 512-GPU pool') is keyed to the wrong variable. It would need restating in terms of how finely the pool is divided by the background workload.

mechanism_reasoning_stated_before_measur: A job needing m servers starts when it is reached in priority order while at least m servers are still unclaimed. What competes for those servers is the set of higher-priority jobs, and what matters is how completely they can consume capacity. Many small jobs pack capacity tightly and leave little residue; few large-ish jobs leave coarser gaps. So I expect the driver to be the GRANULARITY of the background relative to the pool -- equivalently the number of concurrent background jobs -- and NOT the pool size in servers. If that is right, holding the background's relative size fixed while growing N should hold r_safe roughly constant.

E8.design: three arms differing only in how the background job sizes are chosen, each with the same large class at need = m and the same p_m.
E8.arm_A: baseline, as in E7: background = every power of two from 1 to N/2. Class count = log2(N), concurrency grows ~N. (already measured in E7, reused)
E8.arm_B: background fixed at needs {1,2,4,8} for every N. Class count fixed at 4; background jobs get relatively SMALLER as N grows, so concurrency still grows ~N.
E8.arm_C: background scaled with the pool: needs {N/64, N/32, N/16, N/8}. Class count fixed at 4 AND relative size fixed, so the number of concurrent background jobs stays roughly CONSTANT as N grows.
E8.note: arm_B and arm_C coincide at N=64 by construction, which is a built-in consistency check
E8.extra_metric: mean_running (time-average number of concurrently running jobs) is recorded so the proposed driver is measured, not assumed

detector: unchanged. r_safe = largest tested ratio at which the large class keeps flow balance >= 0.9.

predictions.claim: class count is NOT the driver: in arm B, where the background is fixed at four classes for every N, r_safe still falls with N
predictions.falsified_if: r_safe is flat or rising in arm B
predictions.hypothesis: H28 (class count) predicts flat here; I expect H28 to be refuted

predictions.claim: DECIDING. concurrency is the driver: in arm C, where the background scales with the pool so the number of concurrent small jobs stays roughly constant, r_safe is roughly FLAT across N
predictions.criterion: r_safe_C is within one grid step across N = 64..512, i.e. max(r_safe_C) / min(r_safe_C) spans at most one adjacent pair of the ratio grid
predictions.falsified_if: r_safe_C falls by two or more grid steps, which would mean pool size matters in its own right
predictions.note: this is the prediction that decides how v5's practical rule must be restated

predictions.claim: the proposed driver is actually held fixed by arm C: mean_running in arm C varies by less than 2x across N = 64..512, while in arm B it grows by more than 4x
predictions.falsified_if: either leg fails, which would mean arm C does not do what it was built to do

predictions.claim: at matched concurrency, r_safe matches: across all arms and all N, cells whose mean_running is within 20% of each other have r_safe within one grid step
predictions.criterion: no pair of cells with mean_running ratio <= 1.2 differs in r_safe by more than one grid step
predictions.falsified_if: matched-concurrency cells disagree by two or more steps

predictions.claim: arm B and arm C agree at N=64, where they are the same workload by construction
predictions.falsified_if: they differ, which would indicate a bug or seed noise larger than the grid step

predictions.claim: arm B is the harshest at large N: with the background fixed at tiny absolute sizes, a 512-server pool is divided most finely of all, so r_safe_B(512) <= r_safe_A(512)
predictions.falsified_if: arm B is more forgiving than the baseline at N=512

pre_committed_consequence.if_V2_passes: The finding is misattributed in Current Understanding v5. Rewrite it: the safe ratio is set by how many background jobs compete for the pool, not by the pool's size in servers. The practical rule becomes a function of the background's granularity (large pools are only more dangerous because they are typically divided into more concurrent small jobs), and v5's table is relabelled accordingly rather than deleted.
pre_committed_consequence.if_V2_fails: Pool size matters in its own right beyond concurrency. v5 stands as written, and H28/H29 are narrowed to the residual.

declared_unknowns: arm C changes the background's absolute sizes, so at N=512 the smallest background job is 8 servers; whether results transfer to a pool containing genuinely single-server jobs alongside is not tested here
